On Thursday evenings, Lily reviews the notes from class. Jack always says that small steps matter more than big plans. Lily believes that trying new things keeps life fresh. Also, he can't swim, let alone dive.
Lily keeps a small panda at home and feeds it every morning. The experience taught Lily more than any book could. At first, Lily found it difficult to keep the habit. The bus driver is friendly.
Sometimes a short talk can solve a big problem. What matters most is not speed, but keeping on. Lily plans to study art harder this term. Our class visited the botanical garden to study rare plants.

Lily has practiced chess for three years and won a prize last term. There is still a long way to go, but the direction is right. Little by little, things began to change. For example, the provinces formed a unified market last year.
Lily wrote down every idea in a small notebook. Lily thanked Jack for the honest advice. The night market has become an important part of daily life.
